class.name: AudioEffectSteamReflectionSend
class.brief_description: Passes dry audio onward while submitting Steam Audio reflections to an Ambisonic return effect.
class.description: This effect belongs before [AudioEffectSteamDirect] and [AudioEffectSteamSpatial]. Its Godot stereo output is an unchanged copy of its input. In parallel, it folds the input to mono and submits a first-order Ambisonic reflection block to [member target]. With an empty [member energy_field] it uses Steam Audio's inexpensive parametric reverb. With a field loaded, Steam Audio reconstructs a four-channel impulse response and this addon convolves it with the source. The target is the stable [AudioEffectSteamReflectionHRTF] resource, not its transient [AudioEffectInstance]. Consequently, Godot may rebuild effect instances when the bus layout or channel configuration changes without breaking the relationship. The target resource directly owns four dynamically sized channel arrays and copy-adds submissions into them. Energy-field reconstruction and convolution-kernel preparation happen when [method set_energy_field] is called, outside the audio callback. The field may come from a preset, a file, procedural authoring, or a separately run Steam Audio simulation. This effect deliberately does not inspect scene geometry.

method.name: clear_energy_field
method.description: Clears the directional convolution field and returns the effect to parametric [member reverb_times].

method.name: get_energy_field_bin_count
method.description: Returns the number of 10 ms time bins required by [member energy_field_duration].

members.member: A flattened first-order energy field containing exactly [code]4 * 3 * get_energy_field_bin_count()[/code] floats. Layout is Ambisonic channel, frequency band, then 10 ms time bin. Setting this performs Steam Audio reconstruction and FFT preparation synchronously, so do it on a game, loading, or worker thread rather than the audio thread.
Field and impulse-response duration in seconds, clamped to [code]0.01[/code]–[code]10.0[/code].
If [code]true[/code], generates and submits reflected audio. The dry signal remains unchanged regardless of this value.
Low-, mid-, and high-frequency RT60 decay times in seconds used when [member energy_field] is empty. Components are clamped to [code]0.1[/code]–[code]20.0[/code].
Nonnegative linear gain applied to the reflected signal before submission.
Receiver resource that accumulates and HRTF-decodes submitted Ambisonic blocks. Multiple sends may target the same receiver.
